author: BBC News
description:
Overnight drone and ballistic missile attacks damaged Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyhas said, causing blackouts and disrupting water supplies.
 
Zelensky said 12 Ukrainian regions came under attack with the capital Kyiv hit hardest.
 
Nine people are reported to have been hurt across the country, including one child, in the wave of attacks that consisted of more than 30 ballistic missiles and over 170 drones.
 
The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

description:
Five people have been killed after a shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square and around a dozen people are injured, including police officers, Małopolska Police said.
 
Posting on X, the police department said in a statement that at around 15:00 local time that a man who had driven onto the square began "firing at random people from his car".
 
The perpetrator was shot by police and is being transported to hospital, another statement said.

author: BBC News
description:
Votes are being counted in New Zealand, with incumbent PM Christopher Luxon's National Party and Chris Hipkins' Labour Party currently neck-and-neck.
 
Hipkins told supporters at an election night watch party that the direction of the vote is not yet clear, and the next Parliament will need to "work together" and "find a common ground".
 
Meanwhile, the centrist Opportunity Party crossed the 5% threshold to enter parliament for the first time as the major parties see historically low votes.
 
New Zealand's voting system - mixed member proportional - means most governments are coalitions.

author: BBC News
description:
From informants and covert networks to claims of sabotage and assassination, the war between Russia and Ukraine is increasingly being fought far from the battlefield.

Much of that shadow conflict is difficult to verify but BBC Eye has gained rare access to Russians who claim they're helping Ukraine by carrying out operations inside Russia. The BBC has confirmed they are working for Ukrainian intelligence, but has not been able to independently verify the operations they say they’ve played a role in.

For BBC World Service, this documentary is voiced by actress Saskia Reeves.
